definitions.explanation: A large, impressive private residence. Implies wealth and high social standing. More formal and literary than 豪邸.

examples.japanese: {丘|おか}の{上|うえ}に{立派|りっぱ}な{邸宅|ていたく}が{建|た}っている。
examples.english: A magnificent mansion stands on top of the hill.

examples.japanese: かつての{貴族|きぞく}の{邸宅|ていたく}が{博物館|はくぶつかん}として{公開|こうかい}されている。
examples.english: A former aristocrat's mansion is open to the public as a museum.

examples.japanese: {広大|こうだい}な{庭園|ていえん}に{囲|かこ}まれた{邸宅|ていたく}で、パーティーが{催|もよお}された。
examples.english: A party was held at a mansion surrounded by vast gardens.

notes:
A compound of {邸|てい} (residence of a person of rank) and {宅|たく} (house, home). Both characters relate to dwellings, but {邸|てい} specifically carries connotations of high status.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {立派|りっぱ}な{邸宅|ていたく} (a magnificent mansion)
- {広大|こうだい}な{邸宅|ていたく} (a vast mansion)
- {邸宅|ていたく}を{構|かま}える (to establish a residence)
- {歴史的|れきしてき}{邸宅|ていたく} (historic mansion)

More formal and literary than {豪邸|ごうてい} (luxurious mansion), which is more colloquial. {邸宅|ていたく} evokes an image of elegance and prestige, while {豪邸|ごうてい} emphasizes sheer size and expense.
